hero: A bright pediatric dialysis room in a Philippine government hospital. A Filipino mother sits on the bed holding her 10-month-old daughter, who is calm with a small dressing on the lower abdomen. A pediatric dialysis nurse in scrubs and mask connects a thin peritoneal dialysis line to a warmed fluid bag, while a pediatric nephrologist kneels beside the bed explaining with an open hand. A grandmother watches from a chair. Soft morning light, warm and steady mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Why a pediatric PD fill is scaled to body surface area and how the three-pore membrane and fading glucose gradient work.
figures.content: Left panel: a capillary wall with three pore sizes labeled 'Aquaporins: water only', 'Small pores: urea, creatinine', 'Large pores: protein'; arrows of water and urea from blood to dialysate. Middle panel: a dwell timeline with the glucose gradient falling, labeled 'Glucose absorbed, pull fades'. Right panel: two child abdomens side by side; left labeled 'Fill per kilogram: little membrane wetted'; right labeled 'Fill scaled to BSA: more membrane wetted'. Footer numbers exactly: 'Contact area 30-60% of anatomic peritoneum', 'Recruitment rises to about 1,400 mL/m2 (age 2+)'. No dose or order language.

figures.teaches: Where to place a PD catheter exit site in an infant and what to do first for early catheter problems.
figures.content: Top: front view of an infant abdomen with a diaper line marked 'Diaper line', a gastrostomy marked 'Ostomy', and a double-cuff catheter exiting laterally and downward labeled 'Exit: downward or lateral'. Labels: 'Partial omentectomy (infants)', 'Delay 2-3 weeks if possible'. Bottom table with four rows: 'Glucose-positive leak' -> 'Lower fills, lie flat, surgeon'; 'Slow outflow' -> 'Treat constipation, X-ray'; 'No flow' -> 'Check clamps, kinks'; 'Groin swelling' -> 'Reduce fills, surgical review'.

figures.teaches: Outcomes come before surrogates in the monthly pediatric PD review.
figures.content: Two columns. Left column titled 'Review first (outcomes)': icons and labels 'Growth chart', 'Blood pressure percentile', 'Home weights, edema', 'Residual urine', 'Caregiver fatigue'. Right column titled 'Explains problems (surrogates)': 'Weekly Kt/V', 'Creatinine clearance', 'PET'. Arrow between columns labeled 'Numbers explain, growth decides'. Bottom strip: 'Infants: visits every 2 weeks, then 3-4 weeks when growing well'.

card: A pediatric dialysis nurse and a Filipino mother together connect a small peritoneal dialysis line for a sleeping infant on a hospital bed, morning light.
